sentences.text: Aerotitan was a large pterosaur with an estimated wingspan of at least 5 meters. The only known specimen is an incomplete snout measuring 264 mm in preserved length. This snout was elongated, transversely compressed, and toothless.
The preserved snout features longitudinal striations and is highly vascularized by numerous small pits.
The name Aerotitan combines the Greek word for "air" and Titan to allude to the animal's large size.

The remains of Aerotitan were found in the Allen Formation of the Neuquén Basin in northern Patagonia. Aerotitan sudamericanus was named and described in 2012 by Fernando Novas and colleagues. These fossils were found in Río Negro province, Argentina, in deposits from the Campanian-Maastrichtian of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 70 million years ago.
Aerotitan was the first pterosaur of the family Azhdarchidae found in South America.
Within Azhdarchidae, Aerotitan is recovered as the sister taxon of Mistralazhdarcho.
A 2025 study placed Aerotitan in a clade with Zhejiangopterus and Mistralazhdarcho within Azhdarchidae, but outside the subfamilies Azhdarchinae and Quetzalcoatlinae.

Aerotitan lived during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Argentina. Evidence of fish, turtle fragments, and elasmosaur plesiosaur remains in the sediment suggests Aerotitan lived in a coastal environment.
It is debated whether Aerotitan belongs to Azhdarchidae or Thalassodromidae, with a 2018 study tentatively placing it in Thalassodromidae but noting the assignment was not well-supported.
